name: Application CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - staging
      - main

  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  # JOB 0: RESOLVE ENVIRONMENT
  resolve:
    name: Resolve environment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      environment: ${{ steps.set.outputs.environment }}
    steps:
      - name: Determine environment from branch
        id: set
        run: |
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" == "main" ]]; then
            echo "environment=production" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          else
            echo "environment=staging" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          fi

  # JOB 1: PREPARE
  prepare:
    name: Prepare deployment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: resolve
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_DISPLAY_NAME: ${{ vars.APP_DISPLAY_NAME }}
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}
      APP_PORT: ${{ vars.APP_PORT }}
      APP_BASE_PATH: ${{ vars.APP_BASE_PATH }}
      ASG_NAME: ${{ vars.ASG_NAME }}
      AWS_REGION: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
      GIT_BRANCH: ${{ vars.GIT_BRANCH }}
      PM2_APP_NAME: ${{ vars.PM2_APP_NAME }}
      REPO_URL: ${{ vars.REPO_URL }}

    outputs:
      instance_ids: ${{ steps.instances.outputs.instance_ids }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check GitHub context
        run: |
          echo "========================================"
          echo "GitHub Context"
          echo "========================================"
          echo "Repository: ${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          echo "Ref: ${GITHUB_REF}"
          echo "Event: ${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}"
          echo "Commit: ${GITHUB_SHA}"
          echo "Resolved environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}"
          echo ""
          echo "========================================"
          echo "Application Configuration"
          echo "========================================"
          echo "Application: ${APP_DISPLAY_NAME}"
          echo "Application Root: ${APP_ROOT}"
          echo "PM2 Application: ${PM2_APP_NAME}"
          echo "Application Port: ${APP_PORT}"
          echo "Application Base Path: ${APP_BASE_PATH}"
          echo "Git Branch: ${GIT_BRANCH}"
          echo "Repo URL: ${REPO_URL}"

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Find running EC2 instances
        id: instances
        run: |
          echo "========================================"
          echo "Finding running EC2 instances"
          echo "========================================"
          echo "ASG: ${ASG_NAME}"

          INSTANCE_IDS=$(aws ec2 describe-instances \
            --filters \
              "Name=tag:aws:autoscaling:groupName,Values=${ASG_NAME}" \
              "Name=instance-state-name,Values=running" \
            --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' \
            --output text)

          if [[ -z "${INSTANCE_IDS}" || "${INSTANCE_IDS}" == "None" ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: No running EC2 instances found for ASG."
            exit 1
          fi

          echo ""
          echo "Target EC2 instances:"
          echo "${INSTANCE_IDS}"

          echo "instance_ids=${INSTANCE_IDS}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

  # JOB 2: PULL CODE
  pull:
    name: Pull code
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare]
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}
      GIT_BRANCH: ${{ vars.GIT_BRANCH }}
      REPO_URL: ${{ vars.REPO_URL }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Pull latest code
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Pull latest code
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          script: |
            FIRST_DEPLOY=false

            if [[ ! -d "${APP_ROOT}/.git" ]]; then
              echo "Application directory not found or not a git repo at ${APP_ROOT}."
              echo "Cloning ${GIT_BRANCH} from ${REPO_URL}..."

              mkdir -p "$(dirname "${APP_ROOT}")"
              rm -rf "${APP_ROOT}"
              git clone --branch "${GIT_BRANCH}" --single-branch "${REPO_URL}" "${APP_ROOT}"

              FIRST_DEPLOY=true
            fi

            cd "${APP_ROOT}"

            PREVIOUS_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            echo "Previous commit: ${PREVIOUS_COMMIT}"

            NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED=false
            BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED=false

            if [[ -d node_modules ]]; then
              rm -rf "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP}"
              mv node_modules "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP}"
              NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED=true
              echo "node_modules backup created."
            fi

            if [[ -d .next ]]; then
              rm -rf "${BUILD_BACKUP}"
              mv .next "${BUILD_BACKUP}"
              BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED=true
              echo ".next backup created."
            fi

            if ! git pull --ff-only origin "${GIT_BRANCH}"; then
              echo "ERROR: git pull failed. Restoring backups..."
              if [[ "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED}" == "true" ]]; then
                mv "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP}" node_modules
              fi
              if [[ "${BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED}" == "true" ]]; then
                mv "${BUILD_BACKUP}" .next
              fi
              exit 1
            fi

            echo "Current commit: $(git rev-parse HEAD)"

            cat > "${STATE_FILE}" <<STATE
            FIRST_DEPLOY=${FIRST_DEPLOY}
            PREVIOUS_COMMIT=${PREVIOUS_COMMIT}
            NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED=${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED}
            BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED=${BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED}
            STATE

  # JOB 3: INSTALL DEPENDENCIES
  install:
    name: Install dependencies
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare, pull]
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Run npm ci
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Install dependencies
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          timeout: 900
          script: |
            cd "${APP_ROOT}"
            npm ci

  # JOB 4: BUILD
  build:
    name: Build application
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare, install]
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Run npm run build
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Build application
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          timeout: 1200
          script: |
            cd "${APP_ROOT}"
            npm run build

  # JOB 5: RESTART
  restart:
    name: Restart application
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare, build]
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}
      APP_PORT: ${{ vars.APP_PORT }}
      PM2_APP_NAME: ${{ vars.PM2_APP_NAME }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Start or reload PM2
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Restart application
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          script: |
            cd "${APP_ROOT}"

            if pm2 describe "${PM2_APP_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Reloading ${PM2_APP_NAME}..."
              pm2 reload "${PM2_APP_NAME}" --update-env
            else
              echo "Starting ${PM2_APP_NAME}..."
              pm2 start npm \
                --name "${PM2_APP_NAME}" \
                --cwd "${APP_ROOT}" \
                -- start -- -p "${APP_PORT}"
            fi

            pm2 save

  # JOB 6: HEALTH CHECK
  health:
    name: Health check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare, restart]
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_DISPLAY_NAME: ${{ vars.APP_DISPLAY_NAME }}
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}
      APP_PORT: ${{ vars.APP_PORT }}
      APP_BASE_PATH: ${{ vars.APP_BASE_PATH }}
      GIT_BRANCH: ${{ vars.GIT_BRANCH }}
      PM2_APP_NAME: ${{ vars.PM2_APP_NAME }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Check application health
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Health check
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          script: |
            for attempt in {1..30}; do
              if curl --fail --silent --show-error "http://127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT}${APP_BASE_PATH}" > /dev/null; then
                echo "Health check passed."
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "Health check attempt ${attempt}/30 failed."
              sleep 2
            done

            echo "ERROR: Health check failed."
            pm2 logs "${PM2_APP_NAME}" --lines 50 --nostream || true
            exit 1

      - name: Deployment summary
        run: |
          echo "========================================"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT SUCCESSFUL ON ALL INSTANCES"
          echo "========================================"
          echo "Application: ${APP_DISPLAY_NAME}"
          echo "Branch: ${GIT_BRANCH}"

  # JOB 7: ROLLBACK
  rollback:
    name: Rollback
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [resolve, prepare, pull, install, build, restart, health]
    if: ${{ failure() && needs.pull.result == 'success' }}
    environment: ${{ needs.resolve.outputs.environment }}

    env:
      APP_ROOT: ${{ vars.APP_ROOT }}
      APP_PORT: ${{ vars.APP_PORT }}
      APP_BASE_PATH: ${{ vars.APP_BASE_PATH }}
      PM2_APP_NAME: ${{ vars.PM2_APP_NAME }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v6
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ secrets.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: Roll back to previous version
        uses: ./.github/actions/ssm-run
        with:
          phase: Rollback
          instance-ids: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.instance_ids }}
          script: |
            if [[ "${FIRST_DEPLOY}" == "true" ]]; then
              echo "First-time deploy on this instance (fresh clone)."
              echo "There is no previous working version to roll back to."
              exit 1
            fi

            if [[ "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP_CREATED}" != "true" ]]; then
              echo "ERROR: No previous node_modules backup exists."
              exit 1
            fi

            cd "${APP_ROOT}"

            echo "Stopping application..."
            pm2 stop "${PM2_APP_NAME}" || true

            echo "Restoring commit ${PREVIOUS_COMMIT}..."
            git reset --hard "${PREVIOUS_COMMIT}"

            echo "Restoring node_modules and build output..."
            rm -rf node_modules .next
            mv "${NODE_MODULES_BACKUP}" node_modules

            if [[ "${BUILD_BACKUP_CREATED}" == "true" ]]; then
              mv "${BUILD_BACKUP}" .next
            fi

            echo "Reloading previous version..."
            if pm2 describe "${PM2_APP_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              pm2 reload "${PM2_APP_NAME}" --update-env
            else
              pm2 start npm \
                --name "${PM2_APP_NAME}" \
                --cwd "${APP_ROOT}" \
                -- start -- -p "${APP_PORT}"
            fi

            pm2 save

            for attempt in {1..30}; do
              if curl --fail --silent --show-error "http://127.0.0.1:${APP_PORT}${APP_BASE_PATH}" > /dev/null; then
                echo "ROLLBACK SUCCESSFUL. Application restored to ${PREVIOUS_COMMIT}."
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "Rollback health check attempt ${attempt}/30 failed."
              sleep 2
            done

            echo "ROLLBACK FAILED"
            exit 1

name: Run SSM phase
description: Runs a script on EC2 instances through SSM and waits for every instance to finish

inputs:
  phase:
    description: Phase name shown in logs
    required: true
  instance-ids:
    description: Space-separated EC2 instance IDs
    required: true
  script:
    description: Bash script body to run on the instances
    required: true
  timeout:
    description: Seconds to wait for each instance
    required: false
    default: "600"

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Run ${{ inputs.phase }}
      shell: bash
      env:
        PHASE: ${{ inputs.phase }}
        INSTANCE_IDS: ${{ inputs.instance-ids }}
        PHASE_SCRIPT: ${{ inputs.script }}
        TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.timeout }}
      run: |
        echo "========================================"
        echo "${PHASE}"
        echo "========================================"
        echo "Target instances: ${INSTANCE_IDS}"

        SCRIPT_FILE="${RUNNER_TEMP}/phase.sh"

        echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash' > "${SCRIPT_FILE}"

        for VAR in APP_DISPLAY_NAME APP_ROOT APP_PORT APP_BASE_PATH GIT_BRANCH PM2_APP_NAME REPO_URL; do
          if [[ -n "${!VAR+x}" ]]; then
            printf '%s=%q\n' "${VAR}" "${!VAR}" >> "${SCRIPT_FILE}"
          fi
        done

        cat >> "${SCRIPT_FILE}" <<'PREAMBLE'
        STATE_FILE="/var/tmp/deploy-$(basename "${APP_ROOT}").state"
        NODE_MODULES_BACKUP="${APP_ROOT}/node_modules_backup"
        BUILD_BACKUP="${APP_ROOT}/.next_backup"

        export HOME="/root"
        export NVM_DIR="/root/.nvm"

        if [[ ! -f "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]]; then
          echo "ERROR: NVM was not found at ${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh"
          exit 1
        fi

        source "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh"
        nvm use 20 || exit 1

        if [[ -f "${STATE_FILE}" ]]; then
          source "${STATE_FILE}"
        fi

        set -euo pipefail
        PREAMBLE

        printf '%s\n' "${PHASE_SCRIPT}" >> "${SCRIPT_FILE}"

        COMMAND_ID=$(aws ssm send-command \
          --instance-ids ${INSTANCE_IDS} \
          --document-name "AWS-RunShellScript" \
          --comment "${PHASE} ${GITHUB_SHA}" \
          --parameters "$(jq -n --rawfile script "${SCRIPT_FILE}" '{commands: [$script]}')" \
          --query 'Command.CommandId' \
          --output text)

        echo "SSM Command ID: ${COMMAND_ID}"

        FAILED=false

        for INSTANCE_ID in ${INSTANCE_IDS}; do
          echo ""
          echo "----------------------------------------"
          echo "${PHASE} on ${INSTANCE_ID}"
          echo "----------------------------------------"

          STATUS="Pending"
          DEADLINE=$((SECONDS + TIMEOUT))

          while (( SECONDS < DEADLINE )); do
            STATUS=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation \
              --command-id "${COMMAND_ID}" \
              --instance-id "${INSTANCE_ID}" \
              --query 'Status' \
              --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "Pending")

            case "${STATUS}" in
              Success|Failed|Cancelled|Cancelling|TimedOut)
                break
                ;;
            esac

            sleep 5
          done

          aws ssm get-command-invocation \
            --command-id "${COMMAND_ID}" \
            --instance-id "${INSTANCE_ID}" \
            --query 'StandardOutputContent' \
            --output text || true

          ERRORS=$(aws ssm get-command-invocation \
            --command-id "${COMMAND_ID}" \
            --instance-id "${INSTANCE_ID}" \
            --query 'StandardErrorContent' \
            --output text || true)

          if [[ -n "${ERRORS}" && "${ERRORS}" != "None" ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "Error output:"
            echo "${ERRORS}"
          fi

          if [[ "${STATUS}" != "Success" ]]; then
            echo "::error::${PHASE} failed on ${INSTANCE_ID} (status: ${STATUS})"
            FAILED=true
          fi
        done

        if [[ "${FAILED}" == "true" ]]; then
          exit 1
        fi

# IPWiz

IPWiz is an educational developer tool and live dashboard for the [IPstack](https://ipstack.com/) API, powered by APILayer. It allows you to inspect IP addresses, compare IP geolocation with browser geolocation, and see exactly how the IPstack API resolves an address in real-time.

![IPWiz Dashboard Preview](./public/apilayer-logo.png) <!-- Assuming a screenshot might be added later, otherwise we keep the simple logo -->

## Features

- **Live IP Lookup**: See detailed IP information including location, connection details, timezone, and security data.
- **Trace Panel**: Inspect the exact request and JSON response from the IPstack API with a developer-friendly collapsible view.
- **Geo Compare**: Compare the geographical location from your IP address with your actual browser's geolocation using an interactive dark-themed Leaflet map.
- **VPN / Proxy Detection**: Built-in verdict display showing whether the IP is likely associated with a VPN, proxy, or data center.
- **My Grabs**: Persist and view earlier IP lookups using a local SQLite database (via Drizzle ORM).
- **Dark & Light Themes**: Automatic or manual toggling between dark and light modes.

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) (App Router, React 19)
- **Styling**: [Tailwind CSS v4](https://tailwindcss.com/)
- **Database**: [SQLite](https://sqlite.org/) + [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team/) + [@libsql/client](https://github.com/libsql/libsql-client-ts)
- **Maps**: [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/) with CartoDB Dark Matter tiles
- **API**: [IPstack API by APILayer](https://apilayer.com/marketplace/ipstack-api)

## Getting Started

First, make sure you have an IPstack API key. Create an `.env.local` file at the root of the project with your API key:

```bash
IPSTACK_ACCESS_KEY=your_api_key_here
```

Then, install the dependencies and run the development server:

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) with your browser to see the application running.

## Local Database Setup

The project uses Drizzle ORM. Remember to generate and run migrations if you change the schema `app/lib/db/schema.ts`!

For setting up the local db initially:

```bash
npx drizzle-kit migrate
# or use drizzle studio to view data
npx drizzle-kit studio
```

## Learn More

- [IPstack API Documentation](https://docs.apilayer.com/ipstack/docs/api-documentation) - Learn about the IPstack API

# IPWiz - A free What is my IP address tool

> A free tool that shows your public IPv4 and IPv6 address along with the
> location, network and privacy signals attached to them. Powered by the
> ipstack API from APILayer.

## What it answers

- **What is my IP address?** Your public IP is detected from your connection
  automatically. No sign-up and nothing to install.
- **What is my IPv4 address?** Shown first on the page. Most people mean this
  one when they ask for "my IP".
- **What is my IPv6 address?** Shown beneath the IPv4 address when your network
  has one. Many connections are IPv4-only and will show nothing here, which is
  the correct answer rather than an error.
- **Where is my IP located?** City, region, country, timezone and approximate
  coordinates registered to the address. IP geolocation is approximate: it
  resolves to where your provider routes traffic, which can be a different city
  and is never a street address.
- **Who is my ISP?** The provider and ASN that owns the address.
- **Am I behind a VPN or proxy?** The tool reports proxy, Tor and hosting
  signals where the ipstack plan provides them, and falls back to judging the
  ISP name when it does not.
- **Can I look up a different IP?** Yes. Any IPv4 or IPv6 address can be
  entered directly.

## How your address is detected

The server reads the `x-forwarded-for` header, which carries the single address
your browser connected over. Because that is one connection, it can only reveal
one family. To report both, the page additionally makes two requests that can
only travel over IPv4 and IPv6 respectively; whichever succeeds reveals that
family's address. A family that fails to respond means your network does not
have an address of that type.

## Accuracy and limits

- IP geolocation is approximate and is not a physical address.
- Mobile networks, corporate VPNs and datacenter connections frequently resolve
  to a different city or country than the user.
- A clean VPN or proxy verdict is not a guarantee; it reflects what the data
  source reports.

## Other tools on this page

- **Link Grabber** (/link-grabber) creates a trackable link. When someone opens
  it you see the IP, approximate location, ISP and device behind the click;
  the visitor sees exactly what was captured before continuing to the
  destination. Links are scoped to the creator's browser cookie, with no
  account.

## Using ipstack from an AI assistant (MCP)

The ipstack MCP (Model Context Protocol) server lets a coding assistant call
ipstack directly as a tool, with no SDK and no hand-written API requests.

- Endpoint: https://mcp.apilayer.com/mcp
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <your APILayer MCP token>`
- Setup and docs: https://ipstack.com/mcp/

Config block for an MCP-capable client:

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "apilayer": {
          "url": "https://mcp.apilayer.com/mcp",
          "headers": {
            "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:APILAYER_MCP_TOKEN}"
          }
        }
      }
    }

It exposes the same data this page uses: city-level geolocation for IPv4 and
IPv6 with latitude, longitude and timezone; ASN, ISP, connection type and
carrier metadata; currency; and threat intelligence covering proxies, VPNs, Tor
exit nodes and known threat actors. Bulk lookups resolve up to 50 addresses in
a single call. Supported clients include Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code
Copilot, Windsurf and Cline.

## Data source

ipstack (https://ipstack.com), an APILayer product. Free tier available.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is my IP address?

Your IP address is a unique address assigned to your device or network that allows it to communicate over the internet. This tool automatically detects your public IP address and provides additional information such as your approximate location, ISP, ASN, timezone, and whether the IP is associated with a VPN or proxy.

### What is the data source for the What Is My IP tool?

The What Is My IP tool uses IPstack to provide IP address and geolocation data. IPstack processes IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to provide information such as approximate location, ISP, ASN, timezone, and other network details.

### What information can you get from an IP address?

An IP address can provide information such as country, region, city, postal code, latitude and longitude, timezone, ISP, ASN, and network information. The amount of information available depends on the IP address and the geolocation data source. IPstack provides developers with access to this information through an easy-to-integrate IP geolocation API.

### What is IPstack?

IPstack is an IP geolocation API that allows developers to retrieve location and network information from IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. It can provide data such as country, region, city, ZIP or postal code, latitude and longitude, timezone, currency, ISP, ASN, and security information, making it useful for applications that need to understand where their users or visitors are connecting from.

### How can I use IPstack to look up an IP address?

Developers can send an IPv4 or IPv6 address to the IPstack API and receive structured geolocation and network information in response. IPstack can be integrated into websites, applications, analytics platforms, security systems, and other services that need IP-based location or network data.

### Can IPstack detect the location of an IP address?

Yes. IPstack can determine the approximate geographic location associated with an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Depending on the available data, the API can return information such as country, region, city, postal code, latitude, longitude, and timezone. IP-based geolocation is approximate and should not be considered an exact GPS location.

### What can I use an IP geolocation API for?

An IP geolocation API such as IPstack can be used for a wide range of applications, including content localization, location-based personalization, analytics, fraud prevention, security, traffic analysis, currency selection, and identifying the approximate location of website visitors. Developers can use IPstack to integrate these capabilities directly into their applications through an API.

### What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?

IPv4 addresses are 32-bit and written as four numbers separated by dots, such as 192.0.2.1. The internet has run out of unallocated IPv4 space, so IPv6 was introduced: 128-bit addresses written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits, such as 2001:db8::1. Many connections now have both, which is called dual-stack. This page shows your IPv4 address first because that is the one most people mean when they ask for their IP, and shows your IPv6 address beneath it when your network has one. If the IPv6 row is empty, your network is IPv4-only. That is the right answer, not a failure.

### Why does my IP address change?

Most home and mobile connections get a dynamic IP address, which the provider reassigns from a pool whenever your router reconnects, your lease expires, or you move between networks. Mobile networks change it especially often because traffic is routed through carrier-grade NAT. A static IP, which stays the same, is normally a paid business option. Connecting through a VPN or proxy also changes the address this page sees, because the page sees the exit server rather than your connection.

### How accurate is IP geolocation?

It is approximate, and it is never a street address. What you get is the point where your provider routes traffic. That is usually right about the country and often right about the city or region, but on mobile networks, corporate VPNs and datacenter connections it can land in a different city altogether. Use it for things like picking a currency or language, or scoring fraud risk. Do not use it to work out where someone physically is.

### Can I hide my IP address?

You cannot remove it. Every site you connect to has to see some address in order to send a reply. You can replace what they see by routing through a VPN, a proxy or Tor, in which case sites see the exit server's address and location instead of yours. This page reports whether the address it sees carries proxy, Tor or hosting signals, so you can confirm a VPN is actually taking effect.

### Can I use ipstack with an AI assistant or MCP client?

Yes. The ipstack MCP (Model Context Protocol) server lets a coding assistant call ipstack directly as a tool, with no SDK and no hand-written API requests. It serves the same data this page uses: city-level geolocation for IPv4 and IPv6, ASN and connection details, timezone, currency, and threat intelligence covering proxies, VPNs and Tor. It handles up to 50 addresses in a single call. Point your MCP client at https://mcp.apilayer.com/mcp and authenticate with an Authorization: Bearer header carrying your APILayer token. It works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Windsurf and Cline out of the box; setup details are at https://ipstack.com/mcp/.

# SEO notes for the ipstack.com rewrite

This app is deployed on Vercel and served publicly through a rewrite at
`https://ipstack.com/devtools/what-is-my-ip`. Two consequences follow, and
neither can be fixed from inside this repository.

## 1. robots.txt must live at the ipstack.com root

A crawler only ever reads `https://ipstack.com/robots.txt`. Anything this app
serves at `/devtools/what-is-my-ip/robots.txt` is ignored, so the generated
`app/robots.ts` was removed rather than left in place looking authoritative.

The current root file is permissive, which is fine:

```
User-agent: *
Disallow:
Sitemap: http://www.ipstack.com/sitemap.xml
```

Two changes worth making to it:

- Switch the sitemap line to `https://ipstack.com/sitemap.xml`. It currently
  advertises `http://www.ipstack.com`, a protocol and host that redirect.
- Add the answer-engine crawlers explicitly. They are not covered reliably by
  `User-agent: *` on every CDN, and they are how the page gets quoted in AI
  answers:

```
User-agent: GPTBot
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
User-agent: ClaudeBot
User-agent: Claude-User
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
User-agent: PerplexityBot
User-agent: Perplexity-User
User-agent: Google-Extended
User-agent: Applebot-Extended
User-agent: CCBot
User-agent: Meta-ExternalAgent
Allow: /
```

## 2. The page is not in the sitemap

`https://www.ipstack.com/sitemap.xml` currently lists 0 URLs under
`/devtools/`. An unlisted page with no internal links pointing at it is
discovered slowly, if at all.

- Add `https://ipstack.com/devtools/what-is-my-ip` to the root sitemap.
- Link to it from the ipstack navigation or footer. Internal links are what
  pass authority from the rest of the domain to this page.

## 3. Keep the Vercel origin out of the index

If the `*.vercel.app` deployment answers to the public, it is a duplicate of
this page on a different host. Either block it at the platform level or make
sure every signal on it points at the ipstack.com URL. The canonical in this
app already does, because `app/lib/site.ts` hardcodes the public origin rather
than reading the request host.
